label: dioicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its bearing only male or only female gametoecia, the two sexes occurring on separate individual plants.
reason: The meaning is right and it is the bryophyte counterpart of FLOPO:0991072 dioecious. But the text says 'A reproductive quality of' where the parent is phenotypic sex (PATO:0001894), and it does not follow the 'inhering in ... by virtue of' form used by its siblings monoicous (FLOPO:0991280) and autoicous (FLOPO:0991093).

label: monomorphic
reason: The correct opposite of FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic, which has the same parent (morphology) and the same set-of-structures wording. PATO has no 'monomorphic'. 'isomorphic' is an acceptable exact synonym in descriptions.

label: margined
reason: Standard glossary sense (having a distinct border differing in colour or texture, e.g. margined leaves, winged-margined seeds). 'bordered' is a true synonym. PATO has no equivalent, and structure is an acceptable parent.

label: wiry
reason: Matches glossary usage (slender, tough and flexible like wire), and PATO has no term. Texture is a loose parent because the quality mixes slenderness with toughness, but it follows FLOPO practice for tactile/consistency terms. No better single PATO parent exists.

label: callose
reason: Standard sense: bearing calluses (hard, thickened, often pale spots or tips). It is distinct from FLOPO:0991346 callus-tipped, which covers the apex only. 'calleux' is the French equivalent. PATO has no term.

label: appendiculate
reason: Glossary sense (bearing appendages, e.g. appendiculate anthers, petals, or the banner of legumes). The genus-differentia form is fine and PATO has no equivalent.

label: mammillate
reason: Correct sense (nipple-shaped protuberances, blunter than papillae), and 'mamillate' is a valid spelling. It could also sit under rough (PATO:0000700) like tuberculate, but it is also used for a single apical protuberance (e.g. seed or fruit tip), so shape is defensible.

label: flat-topped
reason: Common descriptive term (flat-topped corymbs, crowns, capitula). The definition is clear. PATO flat (PATO:0000407) is about a level surface of the bearer itself, not the level outline formed by distal parts, so a separate class is justified.

label: turgid
reason: Glossary sense (swollen, plump, rounded in section, as opposed to compressed), used for fruits, seeds, perigynia and utricles. PATO swollen (PATO:0001851) is defined as a transient abnormal enlargement, so it does not fit normal taxonomic description. The new class is justified.

label: homogamous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of the bearer's containing flowers of only one sexual kind, such as a capitulum of all bisexual flowers.
reason: Its opposite, heterogamous (FLOPO:0991178), sits under phenotypic sex. The same character must not sit under structure. Also, homogamous has a second botanical meaning (anthers and stigmas maturing at the same time, the opposite of dichogamous). The 'flower' bearer suggests some data use that sense, and this class does not cover it. Those statements should be checked or grounded elsewhere.

label: doubly serrate
reason: Correct sense (serrate teeth bearing smaller teeth). The parent, serrated (PATO:0001206), is right. It is distinct from the more general FLOPO:0991278 doubly toothed (under dentated). The synonyms are standard.

label: spathaceous
reason: Glossary sense (spathe-like, e.g. a spathaceous calyx split down one side or spathaceous bracts). The synonyms fit and PATO has no term.

label: pustulate
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing small, rounded, blister-like elevations, often at the bases of hairs.
reason: The meaning is correct. But its closest sibling, tuberculate (FLOPO:0991060), sits under rough (PATO:0000700). Pustulate is the same kind of surface roughening, so it should sit under rough, not directly under texture.

label: scapiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a scape: a long, leafless or nearly leafless axis arising at or near the base of the plant and bearing flowers at its tip.
reason: The exact synonym 'scapose' does not fit. Scapose describes a plant (whole plant) that bears a scape, while scapiform describes an axis that looks like a scape. The 'whole plant' bearer comes from 'scapose'. Make 'scapose' a related synonym or its own class with a whole-plant bearer. Also, the current definition says the bearer 'is' such an axis rather than resembling one.

label: gynaecandrous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its bearing both pistillate and staminate flowers on the same axis, the pistillate above the staminate.
reason: Wrong parent. FLOPO:0991037 androgynous is defined as staminate above pistillate on the same axis, and gynaecandrous (as in Carex) is the opposite arrangement, so it cannot be a subclass of androgynous. Make it a sibling under phenotypic sex. The current text also contradicts its parent.

label: proliferous
reason: Glossary sense (producing buds, offshoots or plantlets that form new plants, including proliferous fronds and viviparous spikelets). PATO proliferative (PATO:0002102) is about cell division, not this, so there is no duplicate. Structure is an acceptable parent.

label: bipinnatifid
definition: A pinnatifid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes being themselves pinnatifid, so that the bearer is twice pinnately incised.
reason: The meaning and parent are right. The phrase 'pinnatifid lobes being themselves pinnatifid' is circular and garbled (the lobes of a pinnatifid leaf are not themselves pinnatifid unless the leaf is bipinnatifid). The new text matches FLOPO:0991307 tripinnatifid.

label: hemi-epiphytic
reason: Correctly covers both primary hemi-epiphytes (start on a host, roots reach the soil) and secondary ones (start in the soil, lose the soil connection). It has the same parent as FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and is rightly not a subclass of it.

label: pandurate
reason: Correct glossary definition (fiddle-shaped, narrowed on each side below the middle). 2-D shape is the right parent for an outline, and PATO has no term.

label: spine-like
reason: The exact synonym 'spinescent' does not fit. In glossaries it means 'becoming spiny / ending in a spine / somewhat spiny', which overlaps FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped and PATO spiny (PATO:0001365). Spine-like means 'resembling a spine'. Make spinescent a related synonym, or ground it case by case. The class and definition are otherwise fine.

label: fugacious
definition: A deciduous quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to fall very early, soon after it is formed or after the structure it subtends opens.
reason: Fugacious (caducous) is a kind of deciduous, and caducous is already grounded to PATO:0001730 deciduous (generic) in the reviewed union pairs. Shedability is only the attribute above it. Also, 'or withering' brings in a second, non-shedding meaning (evanescent), which should be dropped or kept only in the synonym.

label: julaceous
reason: Standard bryological sense (shoots that look like a catkin because of closely imbricate, appressed leaves). Cylindrical is a good parent, and the shoot bearer (stem/branch/whole plant) is right.

label: aphyllopodic
reason: Correct Carex/Cyperaceae sense (lowest leaves of the fertile culm bladeless, culm lateral from beneath the previous year's leaves; opposite of phyllopodic). PATO has no term, and structure is acceptable.

label: parted
reason: Glossary sense (cut more than halfway but not to the base or midrib; between cleft/-fid and divided/-sect). It agrees with FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite, and split (PATO:0001786) is a suitable parent. The synonyms fit.

label: glume-like
reason: The definition is clear and PO:0009039 is glume. It is used for chaffy bracts, sepals and perianth parts (e.g. Juncaceae, Restionaceae). PATO has no term.
